structure: Part 18 mined all 22 traces from transporters.fit.spec.js in its four describe blocks: transporter list page (8 tests: 7f054, 66d2b, db5f8, f6794, f11a9, 9c144, 40275, 2c405), searching the transporter list (7 tests: 7d16f, 79835, e01b0, 1f326, bdc6c, 21161, a60a7), commercial transporter page (3 tests: a376d, 7b6fa, 0d4a0) and transporter pages accessibility (4 tests: c9d7e, 72c17, b2cb2, 166b3). The spec file was read in full for test titles and assertions. Each trace was unzipped into the part's work folder (t01 to t22, in read order) and read with jq: the action timeline after the Arrival details task, the rendered main HTML at the key snapshots, page titles, the browser network log and the axe results. Every trace walks the same lead-in: stub sign-in, start a new notification, origin, commodity (Felis catus), consignment details, then Arrival details saved blank, which redirects to the transporter list. Pages in order: (1) Transporter details list at /transporters (always, the transporter task's first page) carrying intro copy, authorisation guidance, a Search field and button above a radio-table of every known transporter (Name, Address, Approval number, Type, Status columns), an Add a transporter button, Save and continue, Save and return to overview and Cancel; search states (filtered rows, no-match message) and an error state. (2) Overview, reached after Save and continue on the list or the register. (3) Choose a transporter type at /transporters/add, reached from Add a transporter (owned by part 20; claimed here only for what these traces show, including its axe run). (4) Add commercial transporter at /transporters/add/commercial and Add private transporter at /transporters/add/private, reached through the type question (owned by parts 19 and 20; claimed here only for prefill and routing these traces assert). (5) Search for an approved commercial transporter at /transporters/select, the commercial register, reached only by direct URL after answering Commercial, with its error state. Conditional: the no-match message replaces the table only when a search matches nothing; the register's commercial answer is only in scope once the type question is answered Commercial. Integrations: only browser-to-frontend form posts are visible; no backend call shows in any trace.
